_comment: How the Tribal Lands labels name a Nation, beside the Federal Register name the Impact Briefing always carries in full. nation: the Federal Register name as public/data/tribal-roster.json labelAreas holds it. ownNames (decision DR-247): the Nation's name in its own language, one row per Nation, added by hand, only from the Nation's own public pages and only where the page presents the form as the Nation's own name for itself; ownName exactly as the page writes it (capitals, apostrophes and marks kept; Unicode NFC); page, the address read; read, the date read; premise, what the page says the form is. Never from an aggregator, never translated, transliterated or corrected; a Nation whose pages give more than one form, or only a people's or language's name shared with other Nations, has no row; a new letter may need the label face re-cut (scripts/cut-nation-names-font.py; tests/font-coverage.test.mjs says so). shortNames (owner, 2026-11-13): the shorter name a Nation is generally known by, drawn on the map in place of a long formal name; shortName exactly as its source writes it; page and read, the source; basis, why this form was chosen. A Nation with no row keeps its full Federal Register name on the map. areaNames (owner, 2026-11-13): the label of one Census area that its Nation's Federal Register name lists among several bands, places or communities, drawn on that area in place of the Nation's name; the build pins the area to the Nation (scripts/build-tribal-roster.mjs rule 9), so the briefing and the search carry the full Federal Register name. aiannh, the Census area code; census, the Census BASENAME (a Census rename reopens the row); nation, the Federal Register name; areaName as chosen from its source (the Jev judge and the session, 2026-11-13); page and read, the source; premise, what the source says.

ownNames.premise: The page is titled "The Coeur d’Alene Tribe (Schitsu’umsh)" and says: "The original name of the Coeur d’Alene Tribe was Schitsu’umsh ... This has been our name since time immemorial."
